newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: European gold slightly weaker in narrow range.
newsitem.headline: European gold slightly weaker in narrow range.

text.p: Gold was slightly weaker but holding to a narrow range in early trade on Monday, with the market seen still nervous about the situation in the platinum group metals.
Gold was quoted lower at $343.90/$344.30 an ounce versus $344.40/$344.90 at the London close on Friday.
"We are in a 20-cent range this morning," said one dealer.
Silver was also lower at $4.72/$4.74 versus $4.73/$4.75.
Spreads remained wide in platinum and palladium, with the market waiting nervously to see if Russia would finally start delivering platinum group metals to Japan.
Russia has not yet exported any platinum group metals in 1997. In Moscow, a source at Almazjuvelierexport said Russian officials were in Tokyo for talks this week.
Platinum was higher at $403.00/$406.00 versus $402.00/$406.00, while palladium was at $179.00/$183.00 versus $178.00/$181.00.
